EmailTemplate.subject: Ensuring Your Revenue Cycle Projects Get Done During Covid-19
EmailTemplate.textOnly:
The pandemic has had a tremendous impact on the project selection & implementation process, just like it has in every other aspect of American life. Across the board, revenue cycle leaders have been forced to make tough decisions <[[https://www.flywire.com/resources/how-to-get-projects-done-during-covid-19-an-oral-history-of-banner-healths-point-of-service-implementation?utm_source=marketo&utm_medium=email]]>regarding which projects should get prioritized for the immediate or long term tangible impact they can have for the business and which projects should hit the back burner.
For those projects that have been green-lit, having a concrete plan for how to push them live has never been more important. Ensuring project stability through communication, tight coordination, and resilience have become even more critical aspects than they previously were.
If you’re struggling with how to prioritize and implement high value projects for your revenue cycle or know that you have some critical projects slated for this year and want to get an overview of how others have approached the implementation process, you’ll find this article <[[https://www.flywire.com/resources/how-to-get-projects-done-during-covid-19-an-oral-history-of-banner-healths-point-of-service-implementation?utm_source=marketo&utm_medium=email?utm_source=marketo&utm_medium=email]]>useful. It details how Banner Health revamped their point-of-service process at 29 hospitals and over 200 clinics during the height of the pandemic.
